Who said “This life as you now live it and have lived it, you will have to live once more and innumerable times more…”?

The recorded source

Attributed to
Friedrich Nietzsche
Work and locator
The Gay Science §341
English wording
“This life as you now live it and have lived it, you will have to live once more and innumerable times more…”
Original wording (German)
Dieses Leben, wie du es jetzt lebst und gelebt hast, wirst du noch einmal und noch unzählige Male leben müssen.

The demon's speech in The Gay Science §341. The English rendering preserves the sentence break, which is what makes the passage overwhelming.

Exact wording and the variants in circulation

A quotation in English from a German source has two versions, and they are not interchangeable.

The wording recorded here is the one this archive holds. These are the forms that circulate in its place:

  • “What if a demon told you this life would repeat endlessly?”
  • “Eternal recurrence.”

Attribution notes

This is the thought experiment of the eternal recurrence — and in §341 it is a demon's speech whose purpose is a test, closing with the question of whether you could want it. Readers often present the recurrence as Nietzsche's cosmology, a claim about how the universe actually runs; in The Gay Science it is a condition posed to a single reader, and the later notes in which he took it more literally are a different and much cruder form of the idea.
